To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal design of a large-scale quantum computer involves a tradeoff between hardware integration and reliability and the optimal design of Shor’s factoring algorithm is a quantum computer that can communicate between its qubits with a low infidelity.
the design of a fault tolerant quantum computer can be evaluated using a software tool that simulates the performance of a quantum algorithm on a quantum computer.

the design of a million-qubit quantum computer can be optimized using a software simulator that can (1) search the design space by varying hardware parameters, (2 ) synthesize and schedule quantum algorithms within the hardware constraints and (3) quantify the performance metrics to highlight performance bottlenecks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the performance modeling and simulation tool for the design of a faulttolerant quantum computer and the application of this tool to the design of a quantum computer for factoring large integers.
the design of a fault tolerant quantum computer capable of solving a large class of problems of practical significance.
the design of a fault tolerant quantum computer that is scalable to a million qubits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the design of a million-qubit quantum computer for factoring a 2,000-bit integer in less that 1 month is feasible, but the design of a billion-qubit quantum computer to factor an integer of 4,000 bits in less than 1 week is still a challenge, although the design of a trillion-qubit quantum computer is within the realm of possibility.

a quantum computer with 1.5M qubits and a 10-4 infidelity can factor 2,048 bit numbers in 4.8 months, and the performance of this computer can be improved by increasing the qubit budget and/or decreasing the infidelity.
a million-qubit quantum computer can factor 2048-bit integers in a few months.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a complete simulation tool for designing and evaluating quantum computers, which we have applied to a million-qubit design of the Shor algorithm.
we are able to simulate the performance of quantum computers with up to 10^6 qubits and 10^12 physical gates, which is the largest scale simulated to date.

we have developed a tool to simulate the performance of fault-tolerant, large-scale, and realistic quantum hardware, and we have used this tool to investigate the feasibility of implementing the factorization of 1,024 and 2,048 bits on quantum hardware.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of a million-qubit quantum computer requires a holistic approach to the optimization of both the hardware technology and the algorithmic design.
